celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ﴾ the Resurrection has drawn near, ﴿وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ﴾ it split into two halves, over Abū Qubays and Quʿayqiʿān, as a sign for him ﷺ; he had been asked for it, and he said: "Bear witness." Narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim].

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا﴾ that is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿آيَةً﴾ a miracle for him ﷺ, ﴿يُعْرِضُوا وَيَقُولُوا﴾ this is ﴿سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ strong, from الْمِرَّةِ, strength; or: continuous.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾ the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ in falsehood; ﴿وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ﴾ of good and evil ﴿مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ with its people, in Paradise or the Fire.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْبَاءِ﴾ the reports of the destruction of the nations who denied their messengers ﴿مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾ for them; a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) or a noun of place; the dāl is a substitute for the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form. ازْدَجَرْتُهُ and زَجَرْتُهُ: I forbade him harshly. And مَا is a relative (mawṣūla) or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows (mawṣūfa).

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a badal (substitute) for مَا or for مُزْدَجَرٌ; ﴿بَالِغَةٌ﴾ complete; ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ﴾ avail among them ﴿النُّذُرُ﴾ plural of نَذِيرٍ in the sense of مُنْذِرٍ (warner), that is, the things that warn them. مَا is for negation, or for disapproving interrogation; on the second [view] it is a fronted mafʿūl (object).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ this is the upshot of what precedes, and the statement is complete with it. ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ﴾ he is Isrāfīl; what puts يَوْمَ in the accusative is يَخْرُجُونَ, which comes later; ﴿إِلَى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾ with ḍamma and with sukūn on the kāf, that is, something abhorrent that souls abhor because of its severity, namely the Reckoning.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿خَاشِعًا﴾ humbled — and in one reading [خُشَّعًا], with ḍamma on the khāʾ and a doubled shīn with fatḥa — ﴿أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ that is, people, ﴿مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ﴾ the graves, ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ not knowing where to go, out of fear and bewilderment; and the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يَخْرُجُونَ, and likewise His words:

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ that is, hastening, stretching out their necks ﴿إِلَى الدَّاعِ يَقُولُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ among them, ﴿هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ﴾ that is, hard on the disbelievers, as in al-Muddaththir: {يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ}.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ before Quraysh, ﴿قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾ the verb is feminine because of the meaning of قَوْمٍ (a community); ﴿فَكَذَّبُوا عَبْدَنَا﴾ Noah ﴿وَقَالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وَازْدُجِرَ﴾ that is, they rebuked him with insults and other things.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي﴾ with fatḥa, that is, بِأَنِّي (saying that I am) ﴿مَغْلُوبٌ فَانْتَصِرْ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَفَتَحْنَا﴾ with the light and the doubled [tāʾ] ﴿أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَاءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾ pouring down violently,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا﴾ gushing forth; ﴿فَالْتَقَى الْمَاءُ﴾ the water of the sky and of the earth ﴿عَلَى أَمْرٍ﴾ a state ﴿قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ decreed from pre-eternity, namely their destruction by drowning.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَمَلْنَاهُ﴾ that is, Noah, ﴿عَلَى﴾ a ship ﴿ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ﴾ which is what the planks are fastened with, of nails and other things; its singular is دِسَارٌ, on the pattern of كِتَابٍ,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا﴾ within Our sight, that is, protected; ﴿جَزَاءً﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, that is: they were drowned as retribution ﴿لِمَنْ كَانَ كُفِرَ﴾ and he is Noah, peace be upon him. It has been read [كَفَرَ] in the active voice, that is: they were drowned as a punishment for them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْنَاهَا﴾ We have left this deed ﴿آيَةً﴾ for whoever takes a lesson from it, that is, its report spread and persisted; ﴿فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ one who takes a lesson and is admonished by it? Its original form is مُذْتَكِرٌ: the tāʾ was changed into an undotted dāl, and likewise the dotted one (dhāl), and it was assimilated into it.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ that is, My warning — an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr). كَيْفَ is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and it asks about the state. The meaning is to bring those addressed to acknowledge that His, Exalted is He, punishment befell those who denied Noah as it should.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾ We made it easy to memorise and prepared it for remembrance; ﴿فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ one admonished by it and memorising it? The interrogative is in the sense of a command, that is: memorise it and be admonished by it. None of Allah's books other than it is memorised by heart.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ﴾ their prophet Hūd, so they were punished; ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ that is, My warning to them of the punishment before it came down, that is, it befell as it should. And He explained it with His words:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا﴾ that is, of violent sound, ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ﴾ of ill omen, ﴿مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾ continuous in its ill omen, or strong in it; and it was a Wednesday, at the end of the month.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ﴾ it plucked them out of the hollows of the earth in which they had hidden, and threw them down on their heads, breaking their necks, so that the head was separated from the body; ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ their state being as mentioned, ﴿أَعْجَازُ﴾ the roots of ﴿نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾ uprooted, fallen on the ground. They were likened to palm trees because of their tallness; and it is masculine here and feminine in al-Ḥāqqa, {نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ}, to observe the verse endings (fawāṣil) in both places.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ plural of نَذِيرٍ in the sense of مُنْذِرٍ, that is, the things with which their prophet Ṣāliḥ warned them if they did not believe in him and follow him.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَقَالُوا أَبَشَرًا﴾ accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb); ﴿مِنَّا وَاحِدًا﴾ two adjectives of بَشَرًا; ﴿نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾ explains the verb that puts it in the accusative. The interrogative is in the sense of negation; the meaning is: how should we follow him when we are a large group and he is one of us and not a king? That is, we will not follow him. ﴿إِنَّا إِذًا﴾ that is, if we followed him, ﴿لَفِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ going away from what is right ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ madness.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿أَأُلْقِيَ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways, and without it; ﴿الذِّكْرُ﴾ the revelation ﴿عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾ that is, it was not revealed to him; ﴿بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ﴾ in his saying that what was mentioned was revealed to him, ﴿أَشِرٌ﴾ arrogant and insolent. He, Exalted is He, said:

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَدًا﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ﴾ he or they, by their being punished for denying their prophet Ṣāliḥ.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ﴾ bringing it out of the rock of the hill, as they asked, ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ a trial ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ in order to test them; ﴿فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ﴾ O Ṣāliḥ, that is, wait for what they will do and what will be done to them, ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ the ṭāʾ is a substitute for the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, that is, be patient with their harm.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ﴾ divided ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ and the she-camel: a day for them and a day for it; ﴿كُلُّ شِرْبٍ﴾ share of the water ﴿مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾ attended: the people attend on their day and the she-camel on its day. They continued with that, then grew weary of it and resolved to kill the she-camel.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَنَادَوْا صَاحِبَهُمْ﴾ Qudār, to kill it, ﴿فَتَعَاطَى﴾ he took up the sword ﴿فَعَقَرَ﴾ with it the she-camel, that is, killed it, in agreement with them.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ that is, My warning to them of the punishment before it came down, that is, it befell as it should. And He explained it with His words:

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَكَانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾ he is the one who makes for his sheep a pen of dry wood and thorns, protecting them in it from wolves and beasts of prey; and what falls of that and is trampled by them is al-hashīm.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ that is, the things with which they were warned on his tongue.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِبًا﴾ a wind that pelted them with pebbles (al-ḥaṣbāʾ), which are small stones, each less than a handful; so they perished; ﴿إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾ and they are his two daughters with him; ﴿نَجَّيْنَاهُمْ بِسَحَرٍ﴾ one of the pre-dawn times, that is, at daybreak of an unspecified day; if a specific day were meant, it would be a diptote, because it would be definite and deflected (maʿdūl) from السَّحَرِ, since by right it should be used as definite with al-. Whether the ḥāṣib was sent upon the family of Lot or not, there are two views; on the first the exception is described as connected (muttaṣil), and on the second as disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), even though it is of the same kind, by way of leniency in expression.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿نِعْمَةً﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, as a bestowal of favour ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنَا كَذَلِكَ﴾ that is, like that recompense ﴿نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ﴾ Our favours, and he is a believer; or: whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger and obeys them both.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْذَرَهُمْ﴾ Lot warned them of ﴿بَطْشَتَنَا﴾ Our seizing them with punishment, ﴿فَتَمَارَوْا﴾ they disputed and denied ﴿بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ his warning.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَاوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ﴾ that is, [demanding] that he leave them alone with the people who came to him in the form of guests, so that they could do foul acts with them; and they were angels. ﴿فَطَمَسْنَا أَعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ We blinded them and made them without a slit, like the rest of the face, by Gabriel's striking them with his wing; ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ so We said to them: Taste ﴿عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ that is, My warning and My making you fear, that is, its fruit and its outcome.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُمْ بُكْرَةً﴾ at daybreak of an unspecified day ﴿عَذَابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ lasting, joined to the punishment of the Hereafter.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَذُوقُوا عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَ آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ his people along with him, ﴿النُّذُرُ﴾ the warning, on the tongue of Moses and Aaron; but they did not believe; rather

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كُلِّهَا﴾ that is, the nine that Moses was given; ﴿فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ﴾ with punishment ﴿أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ﴾ strong, ﴿مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾ able, whom nothing can thwart.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ﴾ O Quraysh, ﴿خَيْرٌ مِنْ أُولَئِكُمْ﴾ those mentioned, from the people of Noah to Pharaoh, so that they will not be punished? ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ﴾ O disbelievers of Quraysh ﴿بَرَاءَةٌ﴾ from punishment ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾ the books? The interrogative in both places is in the sense of negation, that is: the matter is not so.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ﴾ that is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ﴾ that is, a group ﴿مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾ victorious over Muhammad? And when Abū Jahl said on the day of Badr "We are a victorious group", there was revealed:

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ So they were defeated at Badr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given victory over them.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿بَلِ السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ with punishment, ﴿وَالسَّاعَةُ﴾ that is, its punishment, ﴿أَدْهَى﴾ greater in calamity ﴿وَأَمَرُّ﴾ more bitter than the punishment of this world.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ destruction by killing in this world ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ a fire kindled — مُسَعَّرَةٍ with the doubled [ʿayn], that is, stirred up — in the Hereafter;

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ that is, in the Hereafter, and it is said to them: ﴿ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾ Hell's striking you.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by a verb which is explained by ﴿خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾ by a measure; a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كُلَّ, that is, measured out. It has been read [كُلُّ] in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is خَلَقْنَاهُ.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَمَا أَمْرُنَا﴾ to a thing whose existence We will ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a time ﴿وَاحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ﴾ in speed; and it is saying "Be", and it comes into existence: {إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ}.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا أَشْيَاعَكُمْ﴾ those like you in disbelief among the past nations; ﴿فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ an interrogative in the sense of a command, that is: remember and be admonished.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ﴾ that is, the servants, is written ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾ the books of the guardian angels;

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ﴾ of sin or deed ﴿مُسْتَطَرٌ﴾ is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ gardens ﴿وَنَهَرٍ﴾ the genus is meant by it; and it has been read with ḍamma on the nūn and the hāʾ, as a plural, like أَسَدٍ and أُسُدٍ. The meaning is that they drink from its rivers water, milk, honey and wine,

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ﴾ a true sitting-place, in which there is no idle talk and no sin; the genus is meant by it, and it has been read [مَقَاعِدَ]. The meaning is that they are in sitting-places of the gardens free from idle talk and sin, unlike the gatherings of this world, which are rarely free from that. This has been parsed as a second khabar (predicate), and as a badal (substitute), and it holds true as a badal of part [for the whole] and otherwise. ﴿عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ﴾ an intensive form, that is, mighty in sovereignty and vast in it, ﴿مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾ able, whom nothing can thwart; and He is Allah the Exalted. And عِنْدَ points to rank and nearness out of His, Exalted is He, bounty.
